the photochemistry of 1-methylthiosaccharyl tetrazole involves two pathways, both of them involving cleavage of the 5-CH2 group, and both of them leading to products with the tetrazol ring opened.

the tetrazol-5-thiol moiety is a very reactive functionality that undergoes photodegradation under UV irradiation, leading to a variety of products, including diazirines, thiocarbodiimidates, nitrile imines, thiocyanates, azides, and cyanamides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photochemistry of 1,2,3,4- and 1,2-disubstituted tetrazoles is very sensitive to the substitution pattern and to the nature of the substituents.
the photochemistry of TSMT, as well as that of other tetrazole derivatives, is highly sensitive to the nature of the substituent at the C5 position of the tetrazole ring.
